newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria to restart privatisation with ship company.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria to restart privatisation with ship company.

text.p: Nigeria is set to relaunch its privatisation programme early next year with the flotation of a shipping company, capital market operators said on Friday.
They said the military government had finalised arrangements to sell the Nigeria Universal Line (NUL) to the investing public in the new year.
NUL was formed after the liquidation of the heavily-indebted Nigerian National Shipping Line (NNSL) two years ago.
"The parties to the issue have been chosen and they will be meeting early next month to conclude the exercise," one source told Reuters.
Capital market operators welcomed the move when it was first made public early this year, saying it would boost volumes traded and attract sizeable foreign participation.
"The volume is such that some of it will be denominated in dollars," Pascal Dozie, president of the Nigerian Stock Exchange (NSE) said at the time.
Market makers on Friday put the value at millions of dollars.
"It is worth billions of naira," a trader told Reuters.
Nigeria's military rulers are widely expected to announce an ambitious privatisation programme in the fiscal 1997 budget due to be presented by head of state General Sani Abacha in January.
State power and telecommunications monopolies, as well as oil refining and steel works are among companies expected to be put up for sale in the new year. ($1=80 naira)
